title: Append to a Delta table

ticket.subject: Please add April to the shared Delta table
body: Our Fabric lakehouse shares `orders` as a **Delta table**: `lake/orders_delta/` holds Parquet files and a
`_delta_log/` folder of JSON commits (open them: two commits so far, both March).
Please append April's orders from `data/orders_april.csv` as **one new commit**. Readers pinned to an older
version must still see exactly what they saw. Don't rewrite or copy files by hand: a Parquet file that no
commit mentions is invisible to Delta readers.
Work in `delta.sql`. The lab attaches the table as `orders_delta` through DuckDB's delta extension (real Delta
reads and appends; creating Delta tables is not supported by it).

acceptance.text: orders_delta holds March and April, each order once

checks.query: SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT order_id) FROM orders_delta
checks.fail: Orders are missing or doubled (all rows, distinct ids):

checks.query: SELECT order_id, order_date, amount FROM orders_delta WHERE order_date >= DATE '2025-04-01'
checks.expected_query: SELECT order_id, CAST(order_date AS DATE), amount FROM read_csv('data/orders_april.csv')
checks.fail: April's rows are not all there as exported.

acceptance.text: The Delta log gained exactly one commit

checks.fail: The log should hold three commits (two from the ticket, yours):

acceptance.text: Versions 0 and 1 still read as before (time travel)

hints: Each file in `_delta_log/` is one commit: `add` lines list the Parquet files that belong to the table from that version on.
`INSERT INTO orders_delta SELECT ... FROM read_csv('data/orders_april.csv')` writes a Parquet file and the commit that adds it.
One INSERT is one commit. Ran it twice? Start over.
